title: Payments docs
intro: Payments takes online payments for your customers with your own gateway keys: Stripe, PayPal, PayFast (South Africa), PayFast (Pakistan), JazzCash (Pakistan), Easypaisa (Pakistan), Rapid Gateway (Pakistan), a generic adapter for any other gateway, and your own manual payment methods (a bank transfer, a mobile wallet, cash on delivery, payment at pickup …). Payers always pay on the gateway's own page or form, so card details never touch our servers. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server (or is pasted into Ecommerce).
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https, and return addresses may point there. These pages use your website's real database and gateway keys, so payments made there are real. There is no test mode: use your gateway's own test keys or sandbox if it has one.
payments: Create a payment with the server token: POST /v1/payments with the amount in minor units (cents, pence …), the currency (ISO 4217), what the payer sees (description), your reference (for example the order id), the payer and where they return (returnUrl and cancelUrl on your website). Name a gateway or one of your manual payment methods by its key (gateway), or leave it out and the payer picks one of the ready gateways that take the currency or the manual methods ready for it. Each payment answers its kind: gateway, pay_first, on_delivery or at_pickup (null until one is picked), and methodName for a manual method. Send the payer to checkoutUrl. Send an Idempotency-Key header: a repeat of the same request within 24 hours gets the first answer again instead of making a second payment (a different request under the same key is refused with 409). GET /v1/payments lists payments newest first (status, and q for an id, a reference or its start, or the payer's email); GET /v1/payments/count counts them with the same filters and GET /v1/payments/counts?by=state|gateway groups them by status or by gateway (none: not picked yet). When you no longer want a payment (for example its order was canceled or expired), cancel it with POST /v1/payments/<id>/cancel { reason? }: it becomes voided, its pay page and the payer's retry close, a manual payment takes no proof, and the gateway's page is stopped where the gateway allows it (Stripe's Checkout Session is expired; PayPal's order is never captured). Money that still arrives (a payer already on the gateway's page, a manual payment you confirm) is recorded as paid with refundDue: true and voidedAt: refund it. A payment already paid is not canceled: the answer is 409 already_paid with the payment, so refund it instead. Canceling again answers the voided payment.
confirm: Never mark an order paid because of what the browser brings back. Payments marks a payment paid only after the gateway confirmed it (a signed notice, or Payments asking the gateway server to server) for the payment's exact amount and currency. Your server then checks with POST /v1/payments/<id>/verify and the amount and currency it expects: verified is true only for a payment of this website paid for exactly that amount, and never for a payment you canceled, even when money arrived after (refundDue: true). A pending payment is asked of its gateway again when you read it (at most every 30 seconds), so an unconfirmed payment is rechecked without timers.
events: Payment events (payments.payment.paid, payments.payment.failed, payments.payment.refunded, payments.payment.proof_uploaded, payments.subscription.updated) carry the payment (or subscription) as the API answers it, and payments.settings.changed says what changed (settings, texts, theme or format, with the setting or text key) (a payment.paid whose payment has refundDue: true is money that arrived after you canceled the payment: refund it, never treat its order as paid); a payment too large for an event (16 kB) comes without its metadata and history. They are kept 30 days and listed by GET /v1/events?since=&types=&cursor=&limit=, newest first, each as { id, type, at, data, delivery } (since: an ISO-8601 time; types: full types separated by commas; delivery: pending, sent, not_connected or failed); GET /v1/events/count and /v1/events/counts?by=type|delivery count them. With the Notifications token pasted into Connections, each event is sent right after it happens (a failed send is retried on later requests) to your webhook URLs by Notifications (turn on its Outgoing webhooks feature, set the URLs and the signing secret there). Each is a POST of JSON { id, type, createdAt, websiteId, data } with the header SS-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">. Check it before trusting the body, then still verify the payment with the API.
gateways: Connect each gateway in the product dashboard (Connections); its keys are encrypted and never shown again. Register the addresses below with the gateway where it asks for them (replace <websiteId> with your website's id, shown in the dashboard's Developers tab). Payers see each gateway by its brand only (Card (Stripe), PayPal, PayFast, JazzCash, Easypaisa, Rapid Gateway, or the generic adapter's own name); rename them in Settings → Words and look → Widget texts. The country stays in the dashboard's feature names. An unpaid checkout on a gateway's page ends after the hours you set in Settings (Merchant payment API: Unpaid checkout expires after, 1 to 168 hours, 24 by default), for gateways that take a time limit, each within its own longest: Stripe 24 hours, JazzCash and Easypaisa 168. A payer who comes back later starts a new checkout from the pay page. Where two switched-on gateways share a brand, the Payment links admin widget adds the currencies each takes. Payers see the ways to pay in your order: Settings → Merchant payment API → Order of the ways to pay (gateway ids and your manual payment methods' keys; the ones you leave out follow, gateways first) and Preferred way to pay (shown first and picked for the payer on payment links and the pay button).
stripe: Stripe: the secret key (sk_live_…, sk_test_… or a restricted key with Checkout Sessions, Refunds and Subscriptions) and the signing secret of a webhook endpoint at the Stripe address below, with the events checkout.session.completed, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded, checkout.session.async_payment_failed, customer.subscription.created, customer.subscription.updated and customer.subscription.deleted. Payers pay on Stripe Checkout.
paypal: PayPal: the client id and secret of your REST app and the id of a webhook at the PayPal address below, with the events PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED, PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DENIED, PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DECLINED and BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.*; check Sandbox for a sandbox app. Payers approve on PayPal's page and Payments captures the order.
payfast: PayFast (South Africa, payfast.co.za): your merchant id, merchant key and the passphrase set in your PayFast account (the API needs it); check Sandbox for a sandbox account. Payments sends PayFast the notice address below with every payment, so there is nothing to register. Takes ZAR.
payfast_pk: PayFast (Pakistan, gopayfast): your merchant id, secured key and the merchant name registered with PayFast; check Sandbox for PayFast's UAT environment. Saving the connection asks PayFast for an access token to test the keys. For each payment Payments asks PayFast for an access token for that payment and amount, then the payer pays on PayFast's own page. PayFast sends the payer back to Payments and calls the notice address below (sent with every payment as CHECKOUT_URL, so there is nothing to register; if PayFast asks for an IPN address, give it this one). Both answers carry validation_hash (SHA-256 of basket_id|secured key|merchant id|err_code), which Payments checks before trusting err_code 000 and the amount. Takes PKR. PayFast's hosted checkout has no refund call: refunds are recorded in Payments; return the money in the PayFast merchant portal.
jazzcash: JazzCash: your merchant id, password and integrity salt; check Sandbox for the sandbox. JazzCash posts its signed answer back to the return address below (one per payment); if JazzCash asks for your return URL, give it this address. Takes PKR. Refunds are recorded in Payments; return the money in the JazzCash portal.
easypaisa: Easypaisa (Easypay): your store id, hash key, API user name and password and account number; check Sandbox for the staging site. Easypay sends the payer back to the return address below (one per payment); Payments then asks Easypay's inquire-transaction API whether it was paid. Takes PKR. Refunds are recorded in Payments; return the money in the Easypay portal.
rapid: Rapid Gateway: your secret key and webhook secret from the Rapid dashboard; check Sandbox for Rapid's sandbox. Payments creates each payment with Rapid's API and sends the payer to Rapid's checkout (card, Easypaisa, JazzCash, Raast). Register the notice address below as your webhook in the Rapid dashboard (Payments also sends it with every payment); Rapid signs each webhook with X-RG-Signature (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body with the webhook secret), and only a signed webhook marks a payment paid, so a payment stays pending until it arrives. Takes PKR in whole rupees. Rapid offers no refund call: refunds are recorded in Payments; return the money in the Rapid dashboard.
generic: Custom gateways (any other gateway, or your own bridge to one), up to 5, each in a connection of its own (Custom gateway 1 to 5): its key (lowercase letters, digits and -; payments and links name it generic:<key>), a name payers see, the https checkout address, a secret of at least 24 characters and, if the gateway can refund, a refund address. The payer's browser posts payment_id, website_id, amount (minor units), currency, description, return_url, cancel_url, notify_url, timestamp and signature (hex HMAC-SHA256 with the secret over the other fields sorted by name as name=value joined by &). Confirm by posting JSON { paymentId, status: paid | failed | cancelled, amount, currency, reference } to notify_url with SS-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">. Refunds are posted to the refund address as signed JSON { refundId, paymentId, reference, amount, currency, reason }; without one they are recorded only. Each custom gateway's notices go to /v1/gateways/generic/<key>/<websiteId> and are checked with its own secret only.
bank: Manual payment methods: your own ways to pay outside a gateway, kept in Settings → Manual payment methods (or by your server with GET and PUT /v1/lists/manual_methods { value }). Each method has a key (stored on payments; lowercase letters, digits and _), a name payers see, a kind — pay_first (payers pay before, for example a bank transfer or a mobile wallet, and may upload a proof), on_delivery (paid when the order is delivered) or at_pickup (paid when it is picked up) — details shown when payers choose it, instructions shown after, Proof upload on or off, and accounts to pay into: each account is rows of a label and a value (bank details of any country, a wallet number, a payment ID …) with an optional currency; payers see the accounts of the payment's currency, else those without one, and only the rows you filled in. Before you save the list it holds one method, Bank transfer (pay_first, Proof upload off) with one account of the rows Account holder, Bank, Account number, Routing number, Sort code, Branch code, IBAN and SWIFT/BIC, empty. A method paid first is offered once payers are told how to pay (an account with a value for the currency, or instructions); until then the dashboard's Overview names it. Payers see manual methods after the gateways on the pay page, payment links and the pay button. Its page shows the method's name, what to do, the accounts, the payment's reference and your instructions; with Proof upload on and Storage connected (the dashboard's Overview tells you while a method takes proofs and Storage is not connected), payers can upload a photo or PDF straight to your storage (allow your Payments address in the bucket's CORS for PUT; at most the Largest proof setting), with their own reference (at most 120 characters); the upload is kept in the payment's history and sends payment.proof_uploaded. Your server reads the methods as payers see them with GET /v1/manual-methods?currency=<code> (server token) → { methods: [{ key, name, kind, details, instructions, proof, ready, missing, accounts: [{ label, currency, rows: [{ label, value }] }] }] } (missing: account while a method paid first has no account for the currency and no instructions; without currency: every account). You confirm the money arrived with the Payments admin widget or POST /v1/payments/<id>/confirm with an optional { reference, note } (at most 120 and 500 characters), kept in the payment's history; GET /v1/payments/<id>/proof gives a 5-minute link to the proof.
currencies: Each payment has its own currency. Stripe takes any ISO 4217 code (Stripe refuses the few it does not support); PayPal takes its listed currencies; PayFast (South Africa) ZAR; PayFast (Pakistan), JazzCash, Easypaisa and Rapid Gateway PKR (Rapid whole rupees only); the generic adapter what its connection lists (else any). Manual payment methods take any currency (an account in a currency is shown only to payers of that currency). The pay page offers only the gateways that take the payment's currency.
links: Payment links are for any amount: invoices, bookings, donations. POST /v1/links with a title, the currency and an amount (or null to let the payer enter it, at least minAmount). Share its url (a page Payments hosts, with every word editable in Settings → Words and look → Widget texts) or place the pay button with data-link on your own page. PATCH /v1/links/<id> with { active: false } stops it. Payers (on the hosted page and in the pay button) and your staff (in the admin widgets) type amounts with the decimal sign money is shown with in your Format's language (else the viewer's; a dot in US English), or with the other of a dot and a comma; a sign followed by exactly three digits that is not that decimal sign could be a thousands separator, so it is refused rather than misread (type 1250, not 1,250). Your staff can do the same in the Payment links admin widget, where the currency is picked from the ISO 4217 list and starts with the newest link's. A link may also ask the payer's phone (phone: off, optional or required; international format) and up to 3 questions of your own (fields: [{ label, required }], answers of at most 200 characters, kept on the payment as answers and shown in the Payments admin widget), and end by itself on a date (expiresAt, an ISO time) or after a number of paid payments (maxPayments): it then answers closed: expired or full, and its page is gone like a link you turned off.
refunds: Refund all or part of a paid payment with POST /v1/payments/<id>/refunds { amount?, reason? } (no amount: everything left) or the Payments admin widget. Stripe, PayPal, PayFast (South Africa) and a generic gateway with a refund address refund through the gateway; PayFast (Pakistan), JazzCash, Easypaisa, Rapid Gateway (no refund call at the gateway) and every manual payment method, so their refunds are recorded in the payment's history and you return the money yourself. A refund's reason goes to gateways that take one (PayFast without a reason gets the payment's reference). A refund records who made it: the member of your staff in the ticket or named by the SS-Actor headers, else Server.
subscriptions: Subscriptions are managed by the gateway: create the plan in Stripe (a recurring price) or PayPal (a billing plan), then POST /v1/subscriptions { gateway, plan, customer, returnUrl } and send the payer to checkoutUrl. Payments mirrors the status from the gateway's notices; the Subscriptions admin widget and POST /v1/subscriptions/<id>/cancel { reason? } cancel at the gateway. The reason (one line, at most 128 characters) is yours: it goes to gateways that take one (PayPal needs one) and into the history; without it, your widget text subs.defaultReason is used, so no gateway ever gets words made in code.
install: Add the script to your pages and place the pay button: with data-link for a payment link, or with data-payment for a payment your server created. The button renders nothing while its feature is off or the product is stopped.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket, each a list beside the selected item: the Payments admin (payments.read: search, a status filter with counts, every field, history and a CSV export (UTF-8 with a byte order mark; statuses and gateways in your widget texts, amounts as plain decimals with a dot and the currency in its own column, times as stored in UTC); refund with payments.refund; confirm transfers with their reference and a note, and view proofs, with payments.confirm), the Payment links admin (links.read; create and turn links off or on with links.manage) and the Subscriptions admin (subscriptions.read, subscriptions.cancel). Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain.
api: Every route answers JSON; errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Amounts are integer minor units with a currency. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off.

build.stripe: Nothing on your pages: payers pay on Stripe Checkout. In Stripe, add a webhook endpoint at the Stripe address of this guide (Gateways) with the events listed there, then paste the secret key and the endpoint's signing secret into Connections. Your server creates each payment (Merchant payment API) and sends the payer to its checkoutUrl.
build.paypal: Nothing on your pages: payers approve on PayPal's page. In your PayPal REST app, add a webhook at the PayPal address of this guide (Gateways) with the events listed there, then paste the client id, the secret and the webhook id into Connections. Your server creates each payment (Merchant payment API) and sends the payer to its checkoutUrl.
build.payfast: Nothing on your pages: payers pay on PayFast's own page, in ZAR. Paste the merchant id, the merchant key and the passphrase into Connections; Payments sends PayFast its notice address with every payment, so there is nothing to register.
build.payfast_pk: Nothing on your pages: payers pay on PayFast's own page, in PKR. Paste the merchant id, the secured key and the merchant name into Connections; Payments sends PayFast its notice address with every payment (give it the same address if PayFast asks for an IPN address). Refunds are recorded in Payments; you return the money in the PayFast merchant portal.
build.jazzcash: Nothing on your pages: payers pay on JazzCash's own page, in PKR. Paste the merchant id, the password and the integrity salt into Connections; give JazzCash the return address of this guide (Gateways) if it asks for one. Refunds are recorded in Payments; you return the money in the JazzCash portal.
build.easypaisa: Nothing on your pages: payers pay on Easypay's own page, in PKR. Paste the store id, hash key, API user name and password and account number into Connections. Refunds are recorded in Payments; you return the money in the Easypay portal.
build.rapid: Nothing on your pages: payers pay on Rapid's checkout, in whole PKR. Paste the secret key and the webhook secret into Connections and register the notice address of this guide (Gateways) as your webhook in the Rapid dashboard: a payment stays pending until Rapid's signed webhook arrives. Refunds are recorded in Payments; you return the money in the Rapid dashboard.
build.generic_gateway: Your bridge to the gateway: a checkout address that takes the signed fields Payments posts from the payer's browser, and a call to notify_url with { paymentId, status, amount, currency, reference } signed with SS-Signature (Generic adapter in this guide); optionally a refund address that takes signed refunds. Then paste its key, name, address and secret into Connections (Custom gateway 1, and 2 to 5 for more); name it generic:<key> in payments and links.
build.manual_payments: Set up your manual payment methods in Settings (a bank transfer is there to fill in: its account rows or instructions). Show them at checkout and on order pages, read from your server with GET /v1/manual-methods?currency=<code>, or let Payments' pay page show them. For proof uploads, connect Storage and allow your Payments address in the bucket's CORS for PUT. Confirm each manual payment you receive in the Payments admin widget or with POST /v1/payments/<id>/confirm from your server.
build.payment_links:
Create links with POST /v1/links from your server or in the Payment links admin widget, then share each link's url (a page Payments hosts) or place the pay button on your own page: the widget script with your browser token and
.
build.payment_api:
On your server, with the server token (or in Ecommerce: paste this token into its Connections): create a payment with POST /v1/payments (amount, currency, your reference, returnUrl and cancelUrl on your website) and send the payer to its checkoutUrl, or place
with the widget script. A return page on your website; before you treat an order as paid, check POST /v1/payments//verify. Listen for the payments.* events (GET /v1/events, or webhooks through Notifications). Optionally the Payments admin widget in your admin, with tickets from your server.
build.subscriptions: Create the plan at the gateway first (a recurring price in Stripe, a billing plan in PayPal). Your server then calls POST /v1/subscriptions { gateway, plan, customer, returnUrl } and sends the payer to checkoutUrl; payments.subscription.updated tells it when the status changes. Optionally the Subscriptions admin widget in your admin.
build.refunds: Nothing on your pages. Refund from your server with POST /v1/payments/<id>/refunds { amount?, reason? }, or let your staff use the Payments admin widget with the payments.refund permission; listen for payments.payment.refunded.
